title: Fairness in Serving Large Language Models
technique: Virtual Token Counter (VTC) fair scheduler on continuous batching, with per-client weighted token-count service

optimized_metrics.evidence: Any two clients f, g that are continuously backlogged during a given time interval [t1,t2) should receive the same service during this interval
Thus, we want a solution that provides not only isolation (like RPM limit) but also high resource utilization.

headline_claim.text: We prove a 2x tight upper bound on the service difference between two backlogged clients, adhering to the requirement of work-conserving. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate the superior performance of VTC in ensuring fairness

reported_metrics.where: response time figures (average first-token latency per client in window)

metric_definitions.notes: w_p=1, w_q=2 in evaluation (following OpenAI pricing); general monotone cost h(n_p,n_q)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: A schedule is fair w.r.t. delta, if for any clients f and g, for all intervals [t1,t2) in which clients f and g are backlogged, we have |W_f(t1,t2) - W_g(t1,t2)| <= delta.
metric_definitions.notes: max-min fairness among backlogged clients; delta independent of interval length

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the service difference between two clients is defined as the minimum of two values: the difference between their received services, and the difference between the lower service and its corresponding request rate.
The response time of client i at time t is measured as the average first token latency of the requests sent by client i during the time window [t - T, t + T].
metric_definitions.notes: T = 30 s; mean first-token latency per client, includes queueing

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Throughput is the total number of tokens (including input and output tokens) processed divided by the total execution time.

load_regime: synthetic clients with constant/Poisson/on-off request rates (overloaded and underloaded); real-trace (LMSYS-Chat-1M) clients
tradeoff_acknowledged: fairness vs throughput/utilization: RPM limits give isolation but low utilization; VTC variants (predict) trade off; strict bound tightening may compromise work conservation (Remark 4.7)
extractor_notes: Fairness is the sole objective; it is defined over token-weighted service, not latency. Latency (response time) is reported to show isolation. Service units follow OpenAI pricing (output tokens weigh 2x input) - an unusual metric basis for cost/service accounting.
load_class_quote: Client 1 sends 90 requests per minute. Client 2 sends 180 requests per minute, both evenly spaced out (§5.2); also Poisson/on-off clients and LMSYS-Chat-1M trace clients
repass_log: FAIRNESS: abstract result (2x bound) replaced by §3 design property (backlogged clients receive equal service)
